output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show PackBridge was already sending a 36-month shelf life from 4 Oct 22:10. No operator overrode anything. Every printed expiry matched what PackBridge sent. The first four Veltranol jobs after the firmware change were correct, including three set up by agency operators. Two Line 1 day-shift jobs run by permanent staff were also wrong.

The ERP audit trail explains the shift. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months for Veltranol under CC-309. The entry is valid from 1 Mar 2027, and the current value of 24 was kept. PackBridge should ignore a future-dated value, but the evidence shows it used this one. I did not check why. The camera only checks print against job data, so it passed every carton.

Do not discipline or remove the agency operators. Do not switch off the camera check.

Do next: carry out the ERP reset and the extended hold. Include the two Line 1 lots in the warehouse. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Inspect retained cartons for HX-15-30 and MR-05-14, which have future-dated edits. Ask IT and Corvane why PackBridge read the future-dated value. Wider 12-month reconciliation and over-labelling are premature. Confidence is fairly high.
